la:verb:depono.gloss: to lay, set, put or place aside or away; deposit
senses: to lay, set, put or place aside or away; deposit
to resign, get rid of, give up
to entrust or intrust, to commit trust to, to deposit or place trust in
la:verb:depono.html:
dē-pōno, pŏsŭi, pŏsĭtum, 3 (
perf. deposivi, : deposivit,; Catull. 34, 8; inf. perf. deposisse, ; part. sync. depostus, Lucil. ap. , v. pono), v. a., to lay away, to put or place aside; to lay, put, or set down; to lay, place, set, deposit (freq. in all periods and sorts of writing).—Constr. with acc. alone; or acc. and locative or abl. with or without a prep.; or acc. and adv. of place where, or apud and personal name; rare and doubtful with in and acc. (cf. Krebs, Antibarb. p. 340 sq.). —
Lit.
In gen.: caput deponit, condormiscit,; cf.: caput terrae,: corpora (pecudes),; cf.: corpora sub ramis arboris,: fessum latus sub lauru,: mentum in gremiis mimarum, et saep.: onus,; ; ; cf.: onera jumentis,: arma,; ; ; cf.: depositis in contubernio armis,: arma umeris,: anulos aureos et phaleras,: coronam, and, shortly after, coronam Romae in aram Apollinis,: ungues et capillos,i. e. to cut off,; cf. comas (for which, shortly before, secuit capillos),: crinem, et saep.: argenti pondus defossā terrā,: semina vel scrobe vel sulco,to deposit in the earth, to plant,; and: stirpem vitis aut oleae,: malleolum in terram,: plantas sulcis, et saep.: exercitum in terram (for exponere), to land, : hydriam de umero,.— Poet. of bearing, bringing forth (as the putting off of a burden): (Latonia) quam mater prope Deliam Deposivit olivam, Catull. 34, 8; cf.: onus naturae,; ; to lay as a stake, wager: Dam. Ego hanc vitulam ... Depono. Men. De grege non ausim quicquam deponere tecum ... verum pocula ponam Fagina, —
In partic.
Pregn., to lay up, lay aside, put by, deposit anywhere; to give in charge to, commit to the care of intrust to any one: non semper deposita reddenda: si gladium quis apud te sana mente deposuerit, repetat insaniens: reddere peccatum sit, etc.,; so, aliquid apud aliquem,; ; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.; cf.: obsides apud eos,: praedam in silvis,; cf.: pecuniam in templo,: pecunias in publica fide,; also: liberos, uxores suaque omnia in silvas, (dub.—al. in sylvis; the true reading is in publico): impedimenta citra flumen Rhenum,: saucios, and 5 et saep.: pretium in deposito habendum,in charge,: si pro deposito apud eum fuerit,.—
To put or bring down, lay upon the ground: scio quam rem agat: ut me deponat vino, etc.,to make drunk,.—
Hence (because it was the custom to take a person who had just died out of bed and lay him on the ground), meton.: depositus, dead, just dead: jam prope depositus, certe jam frigidus,: depositum nec me qui fleat ullus erit,: DEPOSITVS IN PACE,; cf. .—As subst.: depositus meus,.—
Also, because the hopelessly sick were often laid on the earth, dying, given up, despaired of: jam tum depostu' bubulcus Expirans animam pulmonibus aeger agebat, Lucil. ap. : deponere est desperare, unde et depositi desperati dicuntur,: depositus modo sum anima, vita sepultus, Caecil. ap. (Com. v. 121 Rib.): ut depositi proferret fata parentis, Serv.: texere paludes Depositum, Fortuna, tuum, Lucan. 2, 72; and transf.: mihi videor magnam et maxime aegram et prope depositam reip. partem suscepisse,.—
In post-Aug. lang. esp. freq. in the jurists, of buildings, etc., to pull down, take down, demolish, overthrow: aedificium vel arboris ramos, (shortly after, qui tollit aedificium vel deprimit); so ; fin. et saep.: deposita arx,: statuas,pull down,: tabulas, destroy, Capit. Max. duob. 12: adversarios tuos,. —
Trop.
With a predominant notion of putting away, removing, etc., to lay down, lay aside, give up, resign, get rid of: studia de manibus,: ex memoria insidias,: in sermone et suavitate alicujus omnes curas doloresque deponere,: petitoris personam capere, accusatoris deponere,; so, contentionem,; cf. certamina,; and, bellum,; ; opp. incipere,; opp. coepisse,; and with omittere,: deponere amicitias, suscipere inimicitias,: invidiam,: simultates,: maerorem et luctum,: omnem spem contentionis,: consilium adeundae Syriae,: imperium,; ; ; ; cf. provinciam,; ; dictaturam,; : nomen,; : famem,; cf.: sitim in unda vicini fontis,i. e. to quench,: morbos,: animam,i. e. to die,.—
To depose from an office (late Lat.): te de ministerio tuo,.—
(Acc. to no. I. B.) To deposit, intrust, commit to, for safe-keeping: populi Romani jus in vestra fide ac religione depono, 35 fin.: aliquid rimosa in aure,: aliquid tutis auribus,: eo scortum,.—Hence, dēpō-nens, entis, P. a., subst. (sc. verbum, lit., a verb that lays aside its proper pass. signif.), in the later grammar. a verb which, in a pass. form, has an act. meaning; deponent, P.; ib.; ib. sq. et saep.— dēpŏsĭtus, a, um, P. a., and esp. as subst.dēpŏsĭtum, i, n., any thing deposited or intrusted for safe-keeping, etc., a deposit, trust: reddere depositum,: si depositum non infitietur amicus,; cf. : contempto Domino negaverit proximo suo depositum,; Tim. 6, 20 al.

la:verb:dependo.html:
dē-pendo, di, sum, 3, v. a. and n.
Act. (orig., to weigh out; hence), to pay (rare but class.).
Lit.: mi abjurare certius est quam dependere,; ; ; : dependendum tibi est, quod mihi pro illo spopondisti,: cf. .—
Trop.: reipublicae poenas aut praesenti morte aut turpi exsilio,: poenas reip.,.—
Transf., to spend, expend, lay out, bestow upon a thing (postAug.): plus in operis servorum avocandis quam in pretio rerum hujusmodi dependitur,; incassum impenditur opera,: tempora Niliaco amori,; cf.: caput felicibus armis,to give up, abandon,.
la:verb:dependo.inflection: di, sum, 3, v. a. and n.

la:verb:depugno.gloss: To fight, contend or combat hard
senses: To fight, contend or combat hard
la:verb:depugno.html:
dē-pugno, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
To fight eagerly, fight out; to contend, combat violently.
Prop. (freq. and class.): collatis signis,; cf. : acie instructā, * Caes, B. G. 7, 28: multi depugnant gemitusque edunt,: haud procul moenibus,; cf. ; : adversus aliquem, et saep.: Torquatus cum Gallo apud Anienem depugnavit,: ad depugnandum,; so of single combat,; ; ; and as a t. t. of gladiatorial combats,fin.; Asin. Pollio, ap. ; Spald.; in the latter sense also with an object: feram,; cf. bestias,.—Pass. impers.: ante depugnabitur,: so, depugnarier,: depugnatum est,; .—
Transf. out of the milit. sphere: cum animo suo,: cum fame,: morti,.—And in a figure borrowed from the lang. of gladiators: unum par, quod depugnet, reliquum est voluptas cum honestate,; cf.: natura atque luxuria depugnant (flores),rival one another,: indocti stolidique et depugnare parati, * .—*
To fight to the end, stop fighting: depugnato proelio, "the day after the fair," .
la:verb:depugno.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.

la:verb:deprecor.gloss: to avert or ward off by (earnest) prayer; deprecate
senses: to avert or ward off by (earnest) prayer; deprecate
to pray for, intercede on behalf of, beseech
la:verb:deprecor.html:
dē-prĕcor, ātus, 1,
v. dep. a.
To avert, ward off (from one's self or others) by earnest prayer; to deprecate; also to pray, to intercede for the averting of any evil, or to obtain pardon for any transgression (cf. ).
In gen. (for syn. cf.: averto, averrunco, avoco, revoco —freq. and class.), constr. with the acc. (rei v. personae), the inf., the acc. and inf., ne, quominus, quin, and absol.
With acc. rei: ullam ab sese calamitatem,; cf.: ut a me quandam prope justam patriae querimoniam detester ac deprecer,: quibus servitutem mea miseria deprecor? Enn. ap. ; cf.: ego meae cum vitae parcam, letum inimico deprecer? § 10: qui nullum genus supplicii deprecatus est neque recusavit,: mortem,; cf.: non jam mortem neque aerumnas, tantummodo inimici imperium et cruciatus corporis deprecor,: periculum,; Asin. Pollio ap. (with refugere), : poenam,: ignominiam,: iram senatus,: praecipiendi munus, et saep.—Of abstract subjects: Claudii invidiam Gracchi caritas deprecabatur,averted, (ap. ; and ).—
With acc. pers., usually in the sense of praying: quem deprecarentur, cum omnes essent sordidati?: in hoc te deprecor, ne, etc., Cael. ap. : Patres, ne festinarent decernere, etc.,: senatum litteris deprecatus est, ne, etc.,: dispensatorem deprecati sumus, ut, etc.,: deos mala (opp. bona rogare),; cf.: hoc superos, hoc te quoque deprecor,: numina versu,: Dominum, Vulg.

Esth. 14, 3 et saep.—Less freq. in the sense of averting: lecto te solum, lecto te deprecor uno, (3, 32, 7 M.).—

With inf.: umbram accipere,; .—*
With acc. and inf., to plead in excuse: postquam errasse regem et Jugurthae scelere lapsum deprecati sunt,.—(ε) With ne: primum deprecor, ne me, etc.,: unum petere ac deprecari ... ne se armis despoliaret,: spem ne nostram fieri patiare caducam, deprecor, (16), 170; cf. no., β; so, opp. to postulo ut,.—And with the dat. of the person for whom one entreats: deprecari alicui ne vapulet, grex 5.—(ζ) With quominus: neque illum se deprecari, quominus pergat, (but non precarere is the true reading in ).—So very rarely (η) with quin: quin gravedinem ipsi ferat frigus,.—(θ) With ut (rarely): deprecatus esse dicitur, ut se tertium in amicitiam reciperent,; cf. supra,.—(ι) Absol.: pro amico, pro republica deprecari,; cf. ; : arma deponat, roget, deprecetur,; ; ; ; *—
In relig. lang., to imprecate: diras devotiones in eum deprecata, Ap. M. 9, p. 227.—
Transf.: quasi non totidem mox deprecor illi Assidue,execrate, (dictum est quasi detestor vel exsecror vel depello vel abominor, ).—
To pray for, intercede in behalf of (that which is in danger): vitam alicujus ab aliquo,; cf. vitam sibi, Auct. B. Afr. 89, 3; paucos dies exsolvendo donativo deprecatum,: quos senatus non ad pacem deprecandam, sed ad denuntiandum bellum miserat,. Also with personal objects: a vobis deprecor custodem salutis meae,: nullae sunt imagines, quae me a vobis deprecentur,: te assiduae lacrimae C. Marcelli deprecantur,—Sometimes, by zeugma, deprecor is used in both senses, I. and II., with different objects: non mortem sed dilationem mortis deprecantur, Justin. 11, 9, 14; Gronov. ad loc.!*? dēprĕcātus, in pass. signif.: deprecatum bellum,: deprecato summo numine, Ap. M. 11, p. 270.

la:verb:depreco.gloss: to avert or ward off by (earnest) prayer; deprecate

la:verb:dependeo.gloss: to hang down, from or on
senses: to hang down, from or on
to be dependent on or governed by
to depend on, to be derived from
la:verb:dependeo.html:
dē-pendĕo, ēre,
v. a., to hang from or on, to hang down (not freq. till the Aug. period; not in Cic. and Caes.—for syn. cf.: pendeo, impendeo).
Lit.: (anellus) unus ex uno,; cf.: sordidus ex umeris nodo dependet amictus,: dependente a cervicibus pugione,: dependent lychni laquearibus aureis,: galea ramis,: parma laevo lacerto,: hasta umero,: serta tectis,: cervina vellera lateri sinistro,: cui coma dependet,: laqueo dependentem invenere,: dependente brachio,; : nec dependes nec propendes,i. e. weighest neither less nor more,.—
Trop.
(Only in Ovid.) To be dependent on or wait for a thing: promissa tarda videntur, dependetque fides a veniente die,.—
To be dependent on, to be governed by: ex horum (siderum) motibus fortunae populorum dependent,.—
To depend on, be derived from: ex hoc malo dependet illud teterrimum vitium,: haec (membra) ex illis (elementis) dependent, illa et horum causae sunt et omnia,.—Hence of etymol. dependence, i. e. to be derived: hujus et augurium dependet origine verbi (sc. augustus) Et quodcumque sua Juppiter auget ope, .

senses: to dress leather by rubbing and squeezing
la:verb:depso.html:
depso, sui, stum, 3, v. a., = δεψέω, to
knead.
Prop.: id ubi excoxeris, depsito bene,; cf. : lu

tum, : coria,to dress, to curry,: tibi fortasse alius molit et depsit, Varr. ap. .—

Transf., in an obscene sense, to dishonor, acc. to .

la:verb:depello.gloss: to drive out or away; remove, expel, repel
senses: to drive out or away; remove, expel, repel
to drive, thrust or cast down
to drive or push away or dislodge an enemy from his position
to thrust out or remove from a situation, avert
to remove from the breast, wean
la:verb:depello.html:
dē-pello, pŭli, pulsum, 3,
v. a., to drive out, drive away, remove, expel; to drive, thrust, or cast down (class. and very freq.).
Lit.
In gen.: demoveri et depelli de loco,; cf.: anseres de Falerno,: eum de provincia,: aquam de agro,: ab aris et focis ferrum flammamque,; cf.: tantam molem a cervicibus nostris,: jugum a civibus,: vincula a singulis vobis, al.: non equitem dorso, non frenum depulit ore,: qui recta via depulsus est,; cf.: recto cursu,: aliquem urbe,to banish,; cf.: aliquem Italia,; 16,

33: nubila caelo,: ignem classibus,; cf. , and 109: tela,; cf.: nobis aerata tela,; and ictus alicui,: stellas Aurora,; cf.: noctem Aurorae lumina,: cum cibo et potione fames sitisque depulsa est,; cf.: frigus duramque famem,: morbum,; ; cf.: pestem augurio,: mortem fratri, et saep.: quo (sc. Mantuam) solemus ovium teneros depellere fetus,to drive down,: cognoscere, corpora se spatio depellere paulum, push or repel one another, Munro ad loc. (Lachm. ex conj. decellere).—

In partic.
Milit. t. t., to drive away, expel, dislodge an enemy from his position: defensores vallo munitionibusque,; so, hostem loco,; : terrā,: totā Siciliā,: inde vi depelli,; cf. : praesidia ex his regionibus,: praesidium facile, et saep.—
Transf. beyond the milit. sphere, to thrust out, remove from a situation: afflicti jam et depulsi loco,; cf.: iterum ab eodem (sc. Themistocle) gradu depulsus est,driven from his position,.—
Econom. t. t., a matre, a mamma, or absol., to remove from the breast, to wean, ; ; ; ; ; .—Of human beings, . —
Trop., to deter, divert, dissuade from: aliquem de suscepta causa propositaque sententia,; ; for which, aliquem sententiā,; : aliquem de spe conatuque,; for which, aliquem spe,; : te ex illa crudeli actione meo consilio esse depulsum, Cic. Rab. perd. 5, 17: Caesar ab superioribus consiliis depulsus,; cf.: a qua re depulsus,; and: judicem a veritate,nec tuis depellor dictis quin rumori serviam,to be deterred,; cf.: Vibidiam depellere nequivit, quin, etc.,to prevent, hinder,.—
With things as objects, to remove, turn away, divert: servitutem depellere civitati,; cf.: alicui turpitudinem,: morte voluntaria turpitudinem,: duobus hujus urbis terroribus depulsis,: pericula amici,: multam praedibus ipsique T. Mario,: mortem fratri. : omnes molestias,: auditiones falsas,: curas vino,: ostenta a semet in capita procerum, et saep.: quae nequeat ratio depellere dictis. to deny, .—
Absol.: dis depellentibus (i. e. averruncantibus) agnam Percute,; cf. depulsor fin.

la:verb:deprimo.html:
dē-prĭmo, pressi, pressum, 3, v. a.
premo
,
to press down, weigh down, sink down, to depress (freq. and class.).
Lit.
In gen.: vis venti nubem deprimit,: qui (Critolaus) tantum propendere illam lancem putet, ut terram et maria deprimat,; cf. : deprimi in tenebras, id. Fragm. ap. : ad mentum depresso supercilio,: animus caelestis ex altissimo domicilio depressus et quasi demersus in terram,: depresso aratro (sc. in terram), et saep.—Absol.: haec quae porto deprimunt,.—
In partic.
To sink deep, as a plant, a well, etc.; to plant deep, to dig deep: vites in terram,; cf. : plantas, et saep.: qui tollit aedificium, vel deprimit,: saxum in mirandam altitudinem depressum,; cf.: valle in altitudinem depressa,: locus circiter duodecim pedes humi depressus,: fossam,; : deprimere vel allevare rivum, et saep.—
Naut. t. t., to sink to the bottom, to sink, sc. a ship: partem navium,: naves,fin.; 2, 7; : lenunculos,: carinam,; : classis superata atque depressa, et saep. —
Trop.
To press down, depress: animus depressus,: vos, gemi nae voragines scopulique reipublicae, vos meam fortunam deprimitis? vestram extollitis? (a figure borrowed from the sinking of a ship, v.supra, no. I. B. 2), ; cf.: improbitate depressa veritas emergit,: ita se quisque extollit, ut deprimat alium,; cf. ; et saep.: preces,to suppress, silence,: nunc quid elocutio attollat aut deprimat dicendum,: depressus in ludum, i. e. pressed, forced, Asin. Pollio ap. .—
Esp., to depreciate in words, disparage (cf. depretio): adversariorum causam per contemptionem deprimere,; .—
To oppress (late Lat.): populum, Esdr. 5, 15.—Hence, dēpressus, a, um, P. a.
Lit., pressed down, i. e. deep, lying low, depressed (perh. only post-Aug.): humilius et depressius iter,: aquaeductus depressior,: depresso loco castra ponere,.—
Transf., of the voice, low, suppressed: quam sedatissima et depressissima vox,.—Adv.: dē-pressē, deeply; pos. not found.—Comp.: fodere, quo depressius aestivos specus foderint,: pastinare,.

la:verb:depravo.html:
dē-prāvo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
pravus
,
to pervert, distort, disfigure (opp. dirigere, corrigere; good prose).
Lit.: depravata corrigere crura, Müll.; cf. opp. corrigere,; : (oculi) uni animalium homini depravantur, unde cognomina Strabonum et Paetorum,.—
Trop., to pervert, seduce, corrupt, deprave (for syn. cf.: corrumpo, vitio, adultero, perdo, pessum do, illicere, pellicere, adducere): nihil est quin male narrando possit depravarier,: jureconsultorum ingeniis pleraque corrupta ac depravata,; cf. so with corrumpere,: (Campanos) nimiae rerum omnium copiae depravabant,: puer indulgentia nostra depravatus,: ferarum natura malā disciplinā,; cf.: mores hac dulcedine corruptelaque depravati,; and: consuetudo depravata (opp. recta), Müll.: institutum hominis,: inania verba in hos modos,; cf. et saep.: seductus ac depravatus ab aliquo, *; cf.: magna pars gratiā depravata, *; and: plebem consiliis,: corruptos depravatosque mores parens noster reformet atque corriget,: depravatum est cor per mulieres,.— Absol.: solent domestici depravare nonnumquam,—Hence,

senses: to feed on, consume, devour, tear
la:verb:depasco.html:
dē-pasco, pāvi, pastum, 3, v. a., and dē-pascor, ci, 3,
v. depon., to feed down, feed off.
Lit.
Of the shepherd: si d. saepius voles, etc.,: glandem immisso pecore depasco,: saltus,: luxuriem segetum,.—
Of the cattle, to feed upon, eat up, consume.
Form depasco: si haedi roscidas herbas depaverint,; .—In the part. perf.: saepes Hyblaeis apibus florem depasta salicti,; segetes,: altaria, poet. for that which is upon it, .—
Form depascor: papilio ceras depascitur,: miseros morsu depascitur artus (serpens),; .—In the part. perf., ; cf.: depastis juvencis, Auct. Laud. Herc. 77.—
Trop.
Depon.
To cull, select: omnia nos itidem depascimur aurea dicta,.—
To prune away, remove: in summa ubertate (orationis) inest luxuries quaedam, quae stilo depascenda est,.—
To destroy, waste: veterem possessionem Academiae,; so of disease: artus depascitur arida febris,; imitated by ; .—
Rarely in the act. form: et potuit Latium longo depascere bello?: in inferno positi sunt; mors depascet eos, (cf. carpo, no. II. B. 2: decerpo, no. II. B. 2 al.).—The part. perf. in a pass. signif.: ipsaque diris Frons depasta modis,: depasti flammis scopuli,.

la:verb:deprendo.gloss: to take away, seize, snatch, catch

la:verb:depromo.html:
dē-prōmo, prompsi (-msi), promptum (-mtum), 3,
v. a., to draw out, draw forth; to bring, to fetch from anywhere, esp. out of any place (rare but class.).—Constr., usu. abl. w. ex or de of things, with a of persons; poet. and late Lat. with abl. alone, but domo depromere, .
Lit.: pecuniam ex arca,; cf.: pecuniam ex aerario, , and v.infra, no. II.: tela pharetris,; cf. 11, 590: gramina loculis,: Caecubum cellis,: cibum servis,; cf. ; : merum Sabinā diotā,: condo et compono quae mox depromere possim,.—
Transf., comic.: e promptuaria cella depromi ad flagrum,.—
Trop.: e quibus locis, quasi thesauris argumenta depromerentur,; so with ex, ; ; : juris utilitatem vel a peritis vel de libris,; cf.: de jure civili depromptum,; c. abl. alone: sinu vires,.

senses: to consider (as), to count (as), to class (among), to impute
to deputize, to assign, to appoint (formally as a deputy), to delegate
la:verb:deputo.html:
dē-pŭto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
In agriculture, to cut off, prune: vineam,; : arbores,: palmites falce,: malleolum,.—Poet.: umbras (i. e. ramos), Ov. de Nuce, 63.—
Ante- and post-class., to esteem, consider, count as; and alicui or ad aliquid, in late Lat., to destine, allot to any one or any thing: operam alicujus parvi preti,: cum iniquis deputari,to be classed among,; cf.: aliquid delicto,to impute,: omne id esse in lucro, and 21: si hoc in rem deputas,: me omnes esse dignum deputant,; cf. ; Att. ap. : tun' virum me deputas esse?; cf. : vaccas steriles aratro,; : deputata sibi a natura sedes,: servos ad gladium ludi, to condemn, Capit. .

la:verb:depingo.gloss: to depict, to paint, to portray, to represent by painting
senses: to depict, to paint, to portray, to represent by painting
la:verb:depingo.html:
dē-pingo, pinxi, pictum, 3 (
perf. syncop. depinxti, ), v. a.
To depict, portray, paint, draw, represent by painting (rare but class.).
Lit.: tabellas obscenas,: pugnam Marathoniam,: imaginem in tabula,; cf. : depinge, ubi sistam,: idola in pariete,.—
To paint, color: oculos stibio,.—
Trop., by speech or in thought, to portray, represent, sketch, describe, imagine, conceive: formam verbis,; cf. : in illa (sc. republica), quam sibi Socrates Peripatetico illo in sermone depinxerit,: vitam hujusce,: minuta quaedam nimiumque depicta,too elaborately defined,: quidvis cogitatione,i. e. to imagine,; cf. .—
To embroider: depictas gemmatasque indutus paenulas,: auro depicta chlamys,.

la:verb:deprehendo.gloss: to take away, seize, snatch, catch
senses: to take away, seize, snatch, catch
to surprise, apprehend, detect, find out, discover
to comprehend, understand, perceive, detect, discover, discern, observe
la:verb:deprehendo.html:
dē-prĕhendo or dēprendo (v. prehendo; cf. ), di, sum, 3, v. a.
To take or snatch away, esp. any thing which is in motion; to seize upon, catch (freq. and class.—For syn. cf.: invenio, reperio, nanciscor; offendo, aperio, patefacio, detego; incido, consequor, assequor, etc.).
Lit.: deprehensus ex itinere Cn. Magius,: in ipso fluminis vado deprehensus,: in agris,: in ponte,: nuntiorum pars deprehensa,; cf.: deprehensis internuntiis,: tabellarios deprendere litterasque intercipere, Cassius ap. ; and: litterae deprehensae,intercepted,: onerarias naves,to seize, take possession of,; so ; : volucres jaculis,: cursu deprendere telum,: subito deprehensus locutus est,taken by surprise,.—
Transf. of inanimate subjects. So, esp. freq. of storms: deprensa navigia,caught, overtaken by,; cf. Catull. 25, 13; ; ; ; et saep.—
In a wider sense, to catch, overtake, surprise, apprehend, detect, find out, discover any one, esp. in doing any thing wrong.
Lit.: deprehendi in aliquo manifesto scelere,; so, in maximo scelere,; : in facinore manifesto,: in alio maleficio,: in adulterio,; et saep.: dolis deprehensus,: nocte ferro deprehensus,: sine duce et sine equitatu deprehensis hostibus,: (mulier) deprensa,caught in the act,; ; : in mendacio,: aliquos flentes,: agendi subita necessitate deprehensi, ; : aliquem occisum, Suet, et saep.—
Of inanimate objects: venenum,; cf. sq.; : res furtiva in domo deprehensa,; cf. sacrilegium,.—
Trop.
To comprehend, perceive, understand, detect, discover, discern, observe (chiefly post-Aug. in prose, esp. in Quint.): cujus ego facinora oculis prius quam opinione, manibus ante quam suspicione deprehendi,: quid si me stultior ipso deprenderis?: hominum erga se mentes,: falsas gemmas,: quam naturam ejus Pythagoras Samius primus deprehendit,; ; ; ; praef.; : falsa facilius deprehendere et refellere,: quod vix a lectore deprehenditur,: in Livio Patavinitatem,; cf. ; et saep.—
With acc. et inf.: species diversas esse facile est deprehendere,: quosdam mitti,: deprehenditur vitiose loqui,.—
To overtake, equal, imitate: juvenemque puer deprehende parentem,.—
To find, discover, come upon (always implying mental action, post-Aug.): extra carmen non deprendas,: quod in epistolis Augusti deprehenditur,; : apud Ciceronem mira figurarum mixtura deprehenditur,.—
With the predominant idea of restricting the free movement of an object, to impede, to check, to bring into a strait.
Lit.: inter quas (latebras) deprehensus hostis,: in fovea,: flamina deprensa silvis,i. e. impeded, confined,: viae deprensus in aggere serpens,; cf. ; . —
Trop., to bring into a strait, to embarrass: deprehensum me plane video atque sentio,; : deprensi pudorem explicant,: (testes) plus deprehensi nocent, quam firmi et interriti profuissent,

la:verb:deposco.html:
dē-posco, pŏposci, 3,
v. a., to demand, require, request earnestly (freq. and class.).
In gen.: unum ab omnibus sociis et civibus ad id bellum imperatorem deposci atque expeti,; cf. : id non modo non recusem, sed etiam appetam atque deposcam,; so opp. recusare,: sibi naves,: pugnam,; ; : pericula (opp. detrectare), et saep. —Absol.: de proelio cogitandum, sicut semper depoposcimus,: omnibus pollicitationibus deposcunt, qui belli initium faciant,.—
In partic.
To demand, request for one's self the performance of any duty or business: sibi id muneris,: tibi partis istas,: primas sibi partes,: illam sibi officiosam provinciam,; cf.: consulatum sibi,: sibi has urbanas insidias caedis atque incendiorum,: coloniam tutandam,.—
To demand a person, in order to bring him to punishment: aliquem ad mortem,; cf.: aliquem ad supplicium,: aliquem ad poenam,: aliquem morti,: ad ducem ipsum in poenam foederis rupti deposcendum,: auctorem culpae,; cf. Hannibalem,: ausum Talia deposcunt,; et saep.: altera me deposcere putabatur, to demand my death, Cic. post red. in Sen. 13, 33.—
(Transf. from the gladiator's t. t.) To call out, challenge one to fight, ; cf. hostes,.

senses: to weep for bitterly, bewail, lament, deplore
la:verb:deploro.html:
dē-plōro, āvi, ātum, v. n. and a.
Neutr., to weep bitterly, to moan, wail, lament, complain.
Prop. (repeatedly in Cic.; elsewh. not so used): afflictus et jacens et lamentabili voce deplorans,: de suis incommodis,; so, de aliqua re,, § 45 (with conqueri); .—
Transf., of the vine: to weep, bleed greatly, .—Far more freq. and

class.,

Act., to weep for bitterly, bewail, lament, deplore.
Prop.: si ad scopulos haec conqueri ac deplorare vellem,: damnationem illam,: nomen reipublicae, (with lamentari); ; : quae nostri aequales deplorare solebant, quod, etc.,; : ante omnes deplorati erant equites, et saep.: quae de altero deplorentur,; cf.: multa de Gnaeo deplorabo,.—
Since the Aug. per., meton. (effectus pro causa, to weep for as lost, i. e.), to regard as lost, to give up: suam quisque spem, sua consilia, communibus deploratis exsequentes,: deploratur in perpetuum libertas,: agros,: paene Romanum nomen,: diem,: exitum,: deplorata spes est,; cf. vota (coloni),: Jason a medicis,—
Transf., of the disease, hopeless, incurable: aurium vitia,.
la:verb:deploro.inflection: āvi, ātum, v. n. and a.

la:noun:depulsio.html:
dēpulsĭo, ōnis, f.
depello
.
A driving off, driving away, repelling, warding off.
In gen.: depulsio mali,: doloris,: servitutis,.—
Esp. in rhetor., a defence against a charge, ; ; Cels. ap. ; Quint. ib. § 17 al.—*
A lowering, sinking down of the eyes: luminum,.

la:noun:depopulatio.html:
dēpŏpŭlātĭo, ōnis, f.
depopulor
,
a laying waste, marauding, pillaging (several times in Cic.; elsewh. rare),; ; ; : Thracum,: Tiberini fluminis igniumque, ravages, , 3, 31; . In plur., .

senses: to ravage, devastate, destroy, lay waste
la:verb:depopulor.html:
dē-pŏpŭlor, ātus, 1,
v. dep. a., to lay waste, ravage, plunder, pillage (class.).
Prop.: ut Ambiorigis fines depopularentur,; cf.: ad fines depopulandos,; ; : agros,; ; et saep.; cf.: extrema agri Romani,: eam regionem,: vicinam humum late, et saep.: multas domos, plurimas urbes, omnia fana,: quos fidos nobis rebatur,.—
Transf., in gen., to waste, lay waste, dissipate, destroy, sweep away: quos impune depopulatur et dispoliatur dedecus, Afran. ap. : Cerealia dona,: hereditates,: in qua (sc. urbe) omne mortalium genus vis pestilentiae depopulabatur,: aras,.!*?
Active form dēpopulo, āre: agros audaces depopulant servi, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 3 Rib.): macellum, (Com. v. 13 Rib.): agros provinciamque, Auct. B. Hisp. 42, 6: greges,.—
depopulor, ari, in pass. signif.: communi latrocinio terra omnis depopulabitur,: depopulata est regio,. In class. lang. only in the Part. perf.: depopulatis agris,laid waste,: depopulata Gallia,; late depopulato agro,: omnis ora maritima depopulata ab Achaeis erat, 37, 4: regiones, et saep.; Justin. 42, 2; .

la:noun:depositio.html:
dēpŏsĭtĭo, ōnis, f.
depono
(post-Aug.; most freq. in jurid. Lat.).
Lit., a laying down, putting off.
A depositing for safe-keeping, ; ; .—
A pulling or tearing down: aedificii,.—
A depositing in the earth, burying, (of 384 A.D.).—
A parting from, getting rid of: carnis sordium, Pet. 3, 21; cf.: tabernaculi mei,i. e. the body, Pet. 1, 14.—
Trop.
In gen.: testium, a deposition, testimony, Cod. 2, 43, 3: dignitatis, alowering, degradation, —
In rhetor.
The close of a period: prout aut depositio aut inceptio aut transitus postulabit, Spald.—
The lowering of voice, sound, or speed of utterance, = Gr. θέσις (opp. ἄρσις = elatio), .

la:verb:depravo#2.html:
dē-prāvo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
pravus
,
to pervert, distort, disfigure (opp. dirigere, corrigere; good prose).
Lit.: depravata corrigere crura, Müll.; cf. opp. corrigere,; : (oculi) uni animalium homini depravantur, unde cognomina Strabonum et Paetorum,.—
Trop., to pervert, seduce, corrupt, deprave (for syn. cf.: corrumpo, vitio, adultero, perdo, pessum do, illicere, pellicere, adducere): nihil est quin male narrando possit depravarier,: jureconsultorum ingeniis pleraque corrupta ac depravata,; cf. so with corrumpere,: (Campanos) nimiae rerum omnium copiae depravabant,: puer indulgentia nostra depravatus,: ferarum natura malā disciplinā,; cf.: mores hac dulcedine corruptelaque depravati,; and: consuetudo depravata (opp. recta), Müll.: institutum hominis,: inania verba in hos modos,; cf. et saep.: seductus ac depravatus ab aliquo, *; cf.: magna pars gratiā depravata, *; and: plebem consiliis,: corruptos depravatosque mores parens noster reformet atque corriget,: depravatum est cor per mulieres,.— Absol.: solent domestici depravare nonnumquam,—Hence,

la:verb:deporto.html:
dē-porto, āvi, ātum, 1 (
arch. inf. pass. deportarier, ), v. a., to carry or convey down; to carry off, to convey away (freq. and good prose).
In gen.: de fundo tigna et oleam ne deportato,: arma Brundisium jumentis, Pomp. ap. A. fin.: frumentum in castra. : ossa ejus in Cappadociam ad matrem,: corpus Augusti Romam,; cf. : aliquem per vicos,fin. et saep.:

ut te Leucadem deportaret, : naves partem exercitus eo deportaverant,; so of transporting by water,; ; : quos (serpentes) flumina deportant,: lucem,: arcam,. —

In partic. as a t. t.
To bring or fetch home any thing from the provinces: victorem exercitum,; so ; fin. al.: Tertia tua, quam tu tecum deportaras,: cum aliud nihil ex tanta praeda domum suam deportavisset,.—
Transf., of abstract objects, to carry away, i. e. to get, acquire: tertium triumphum,; cf. lauream,; and: gloriam ex illis gentibus,: si nihil aliud de hac provincia nisi illius benevolentiam deportassem,: te (sc. Atticum) non cognomen solum Athenis deportasse, sed humanitatem et prudentiam intellego,: nihil ex ista provincia potes, quod jucundius sit, deportare,: ex Asia deportatum flagitium ac dedecus,.—
To banish, transport, for life (attended with loss of citizenship and testatorship, both of which the relegatus retained, v. ; —mostly post-Aug.— for syn. also cf.: exsilio afficio or multo, in exsilium pello or eicio, expello, exigo): inter poenas est etiam insulae deportatio, quae poena adimit civitatem Romanam, etc.,: Vibius Serenus in insulam Amorgum deportatur,: ut liberti quoque Italia deportarentur,: in reis deportatis,.—
Transf.: non hoc publicitus scelus hinc deportarier In solas terras?.

la:noun:depravatio.html:
dēprāvātĭo, ōnis, f.
depravo
,
a perverting, distorting, corrupting, vitiating (freq. in Cic.; elsewh. rare).
Lit.: distortio et depravatio quaedam (membrorum),; cf.: pedum, manuum, articulorum omnium depravationes,: oris,.—
Trop.: depravatio et foeditas animi (c. c. deformitas corporis),: verbi,: consuetudinum,.—Absol.: nostra (c. c. superstitio),perversity,.

la:verb:deputo#2.html:
dē-pŭto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
In agriculture, to cut off, prune: vineam,; : arbores,: palmites falce,: malleolum,.—Poet.: umbras (i. e. ramos), Ov. de Nuce, 63.—
Ante- and post-class., to esteem, consider, count as; and alicui or ad aliquid, in late Lat., to destine, allot to any one or any thing: operam alicujus parvi preti,: cum iniquis deputari,to be classed among,; cf.: aliquid delicto,to impute,: omne id esse in lucro, and 21: si hoc in rem deputas,: me omnes esse dignum deputant,; cf. ; Att. ap. : tun' virum me deputas esse?; cf. : vaccas steriles aratro,; : deputata sibi a natura sedes,: servos ad gladium ludi, to condemn, Capit. .

la:verb:depereo.gloss: to perish, to be ruined, to get lost, to go awaste
senses: to perish, to be ruined, to get lost, to go awaste
to be desperately in love with, to love to distraction
la:verb:depereo.html:
dē-pĕrĕo, ii (
fut. deperiet for -ibit, ), 4, v. n., to go to ruin, perish, die; to be lost, undone.
In gen. (class.): neque adaugescit quicquam neque deperit inde (sc. de materia),: tempestate naves,: perexigua pars illius exercitus superest, magna pars deperiit,; cf. : si servus deperisset, had been lost (by death or flight), : ut scida ne qua depereat,: qui deperiit minor uno mense vel anno,has died, et saep.: (auro) rerum uni nihil igne deperit,: decor vultus ejus deperiit,faded,.—
In partic., to be desperately in love with, dying with love for a person (not in Cic., neither in Verg., Hor., nor Ovid, but freq. in Plaut.).—Constr.: aliquem (amore), more rarely alicujus amore, in aliquo; and absol.: ut hic te efflictim deperit,: aliquam (with deamare),: aliquam,; et saep.; ; Catull. 100, 2: amore aliquam deperire,; cf.: illum deperit impotente amore, Catull. 35, 12: amore mulierculae,; cf.: amore sui,: cum laceratum corpus, in quo deperibat, intueretur,.—Absol.: rogas? deperit,.

dēprĕcātĭo, ōnis, f.

a warding off or averting by prayer; a deprecating, deprecation.
Prop.
In gen.: periculi. Cic. Rab. perd. 9, 26: venia deprecationis, Quint. prooem. § 2.—
Esp., in relig. lang., an imprecation: defigi diris deprecationibus,: deorum,an invoking of the gods to send punishment on the perjurer,; .—More freq.,

dēpŭdet, ŭit, 2,
v. impers. *
To be greatly ashamed: cum eum non depuderet mare infestare,—
Not to be ashamed, to become shameless (perh. not ante-Aug.; very rare): depuduit,: assiduis conviciis depudere didicerat,.

la:noun:depulsor.html:
dēpulsor, ōris, m.
id.
,
one who drives away, removes, repels (rare): dominatus, * : malorum,: alius vel servator honorum vel malorum depulsor, Boëth. Cons. Phil. 4, 6.—In inscriptions, an epithet of Jupiter, as the averter of evil (cf. Averruncus),

la:noun:depositor.html:
dēpŏsĭtor, ōris, m.
id.
(post-Aug. and very rare).
One who deposits a thing for safe-keeping, a depositor, .—
One who disowns or disclaims: patris natique,.

la:verb:deperdo.html:
dē-perdo, dĭdi, dĭtum, 3,
v a.
To destroy, ruin (so only in the part. perf., and rare): sator inopia deperditus,i. e. impoverished,: ut est deperditus Io,i. e. desperately in love, (3, 28, 29 M.); cf. amore,: deperditum intelligitur, quod in rerum natura esse desiit,.—More freq. and class.,
To lose: qui non solum bona sed etiam honestatem miseri deperdiderunt,: nihil sui,: vitalem sensum,: folia (arbores),: colorem,: gratiam,: tantum ejus opinionis,: bonam famam,: usum linguae,: ne quid ex his deperdat,; cf.: paucos ex suis (nostri),: ne quid apud vos de existimatione sua deperderet,; so, quid de libertate,: nihil de jure civitatis,: paululum admodum de celeritate (stilus),: ne quid Summa deperdat metuens, aut ampliet ut rem,: quod ex naufragio expulsum est ... non est in derelicto, sed in deperdito,; cf. (for the pass. of deperdo, depereo is used).—Hence, * dēperdĭtus, a, um, P. a. (acc. to no. II.), corrupt, abandoned, .

to dishonor, Hier. in Nahum. c. 3.

la:verb:depeculor.html:
dē-pĕcūlor, ātus (and old
Act. fut. infin. depeculassere, Lucil. ap. ; cf. Neue, Form. 2, 421, and v.infra), 1, v. dep. a. [peculium], to despoil, pillage, rifle, plunder, embezzle (very rare).
Prop.: Apollonium omni argento spoliasti ac depeculatus es,.—

la:verb:depeciscor.gloss: to bargain for; to come to terms
senses: to bargain for; to come to terms
la:verb:depeciscor.html:
dēpĕciscor, -pectus, or dēpăciscor, pactus, 3,
v. dep. a. [de-paciscor], to bargain for, agree upon; and absol., to make an agreement.
Lit. (repeatedly in Cic., elsewh. rare): ipse tria praedia sibi depectus est,: cum illo partem suam depecisci,: aliquid cum aliquo,; cf.: depectus est cum eis, ut arma et impedimenta relinqueret,: ad condiciones alicujus,—
With jurists, in a bad sense, acc. to : hoc edicto tenetur etiam is, qui depectus est. Depectus autem dicitur turpiter pactus.—*
Trop., with abl. rei: jam depecisci morte cupio, to bargain for death, i. e. I am content to die, ; cf.: cur non honestissimo (sc. periculo) depecisci velim?, v. paciscor, no. II.
